deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics: no formulas, derivations or computations. Two layers of writing are visible.

(a) The dark, legible script is mirror-reversed. It is show-through of the recto, page 107. Readable fragments match the page-107 transcription closely, for example 'dem Vorbilde der Nicht-Euklidischen Geometrie', 'die Grundlagen der Mechanik, Optik etc. in Formen [von Axiomen]', 'Wissengebiet umfassend, dann durch Adjunction', 'eines gewissen invarianten Begriffes', 'des imaginären Kugelkreises', 'Das Hermannsche Problem ist die Entzifferung von Melodien, Partituren', 'des Textes, allein aus der resultirenden phonographischen Curve', 'Hymne auf den Kreis!', 'Variationsrechnung, Mechanik, Algebra, Zahlentheorie', 'Irrationalität von π', 'Mathematik darin besteht ohne alle Instrumente'. Even the reversed folio number '107' and the 'Allgemein Mathem.' heading show through at the top. The machine transcription picked up these bled-through words; they are not content of folio 108.

(b) The genuine content of folio 108 is a very faint, upright pencil text. It appears to continue page 107's 'Hymne auf den Kreis' passage. Page 107 breaks off at 'Wie grade der hohe Reiz der Mathematik darin besteht ohne alle Instrumente'. The faint text seems to continue roughly as '[Experimente] der Physiker, Chemiker gemacht, ohne materielle oder technische Verhältnisse, ohne Quellenstudien wie sie der Historiker [braucht] ...'. Further down are fragments such as '... Kenntnis ...', '... Sinn ...', '... gehandhabten ...', '... Unterschied zwischen Kunst und Wissenschaft ...', and '... mehr die Form, das Formale ... die künstlerische Gestaltung die Hauptsache ...'.

The theme is philosophical. Hilbert is praising pure mathematics, using the circle as his example, for its independence from instruments, experiments and source studies. He then compares mathematics with art, where form is the main thing. Most of the faint text is illegible in this image, and the readings above are tentative.

results.what: Philosophical remark that the charm of mathematics (illustrated by the circle) lies in reaching results without instruments, experiments or historical source studies, and a comparison of mathematics with art, where form is the main thing
results.modern_name: Philosophy of mathematics: autonomy and aesthetic character of pure mathematics
results.usually_credited_to: General 19th-century theme; Hilbert voiced similar views in later lectures and addresses
